And they seem righteous outwardly, not in the eyes of such as the Scripture calls Gods, (Ps. 82:6.) but of such only as die like men.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
Without just cause He seems to utter denunciations against those who build the sepulchres of the Prophets; for so far what they did was praiseworthy; how then do they deserve this woe?

And in the prophetic writings, the historical sense is the body, the spiritual meaning is the soul; the sepulchres are the letter and books themselves of Scripture. They then who attend only to the historical meaning, honour the bodies of the Prophets, and set in the letter as in a sepulchre; and are called Pharisees, i. e. 'cut off,' as it were cutting off the soul of the Prophets from their body.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the just, and you say: if we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets. therefore you bear witness to yourselves that you are the sons of those who killed the prophets. And you, fill up the measure of your fathers. Serpents, brood of vipers, how will you flee from the judgment of Gehenna? therefore, behold, I send to you prophets and wise men and scribes; some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and you will persecute them from city to city, that upon you may come all the just blood which is poured out upon the earth, from the blood of Abel the just to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar. Amen, I say to you: all these things will come upon this generation.

As far as the surface of the text is concerned, he does not seem to threaten with sufficient reason against those who build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the just. For as far as this alone goes, they were doing something praiseworthy, in that they built the tombs of the prophets and adorned the monuments of the just. They did not consent to the works of their fathers, by which those had dared to act against the prophets and the saints, especially in that they say: if we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets. How then were they worthy to incur the woe? But if someone speaks thus: as far indeed as that deed and the profession of their words go, they were not guilty, but they were culpable on account of this, that they bore witness to themselves that they were the sons of those who killed the prophets — this too is not true. For in a matter which does not fall under a man's choice, how can a man become guilty? For it is not within the choice of each individual man whose son he is, of a good man or of a bad man.

Therefore neither because they built the tombs of the prophets and said: if we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been guilty, were they either guilty or innocent; but because by the very facts and by the likeness of their crimes they bore witness to themselves that they were the sons of those who killed the prophets, filling up the measure of their fathers and adding still what had been lacking, supplying by the killing of Christ the Son of God the killing of the prophets and the just. On account of which it was not possible for those who were held liable by such a deed to flee from the judgment of Gehenna: for whom not even the blood of Christ was enough, but they still killed and crucified those prophets or scribes who had been sent by Christ, and scourged them in their synagogues and persecuted them from city to city. For all which murderous deeds committed it was just that they should suffer the destruction of Jerusalem and the captivity of the people, since the patience of God no longer bore the greatness and the multitude of their crimes. But there came upon their generation, who had filled up the measure of their fathers and had heaped upon them the prophets and wise men and scribes of Jesus Christ, all the just blood which is poured out upon the earth, from the blood of Abel the just to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whose killing he imputes to the scribes and Pharisees, as though he had not been killed by their fathers but by those very men; for so it is written: whom you killed between the temple and the altar.

But those who are reproached by Christ cannot have killed Zechariah son of Barachiah from among the twelve prophets, whose writings we have in our hands: rather, he means Zechariah the father of John, concerning whom, indeed, we cannot show through the canonical scriptures either that he was the son of Barachiah or that the scribes and Pharisees killed him between the temple and the altar. But there has come to us a certain tradition of this sort: that there is a certain place in the temple where indeed it is permitted for virgins to stand and pray to God, but women who had had experience of the marriage bed were not permitted to stand in it. Now Mary, after she had borne the Savior, entering to worship stood in that place of the virgins; and when those who knew that she had already borne a son were forbidding her, Zechariah stood and said to those forbidding her that she was worthy of the place of the virgins, since she was still a virgin. Therefore, as though most manifestly Zechariah were acting against the law and permitting a woman to stand in the place of the virgins, the men of that generation killed him between the temple and the altar.

Yet from those who do not believe a tradition of this sort, let us demand a reason, how Jesus reproaches them on account of Zechariah not as sons of those who killed, besides the prophets, Zechariah also, but as those who themselves killed Zechariah between the temple and the altar. If, therefore, the word of Christ is true which he speaks to the Pharisees and scribes then present: whom you killed between the temple and the altar, it is not possible that he be understood to be that Zechariah who is one of the twelve. Nor yet is it any wonder if it happened that both "Zechariah" and their fathers were of the same name.

The discourse which Christ speaks wishes to say something of this sort: that you who excuse yourselves from the blood of the prophets and say: if we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been their partners in the blood of the prophets, and build the tombs of the prophets who were killed, by these very things which you have dared against me, bear witness to yourselves that you are the sons of your murderous fathers, filling up by my blood and the blood of my prophets what had been lacking to their iniquities. For they did not crucify Christ, but you have crucified him, filling it up and having become the offspring of those vipers who killed the prophets, worst serpents, shutting off from yourselves the way of flight from the judgment of Gehenna on account of the greatness of the crimes which you have committed against Christ and against his wise men and against his prophets and against his scribes, and yet you have dared to sever yourselves from the fellowship of your fathers and to excuse yourselves from the blood of the prophets.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
But it follows consequently that someone who understands the scriptures according to the simple history might raise an objection and inquire why he did not say "as far as the blood of John the son of Zechariah," especially since "the law and the prophets prophesied until John." To him we shall say that the matter is manifest: that it was not the scribes and Pharisees who killed John, but Herod. For even though the scribes and Pharisees did not believe John (as it is written: "if we say, from heaven, he will say to us: why then did you not believe him?"), nevertheless they still had a certain reverence for his name, not daring to say, in response to Christ's question about his baptism, that it was from men; for they feared the people, who believed that "John was truly a prophet." How then would he reproach, as though they were his murderers, those who did not kill John? But he reproached them as the murderers of Zechariah, saying: whom you killed between the temple and the altar.

Further, regarding the text, it must be said that the generation of sinners is not punished immediately, as soon as the sin has been committed, but when the following generation, which ought to correct in itself the sin of its fathers, has instead added worse things to the sins of its fathers; and thus, if many generations have sinned in some nation or in a city, the nation is punished or the city is destroyed. So therefore also the nation of the Jews, inflicting many evils upon the prophets, was not to be punished immediately, as it began the murder against them, but after the patience of God, after they had added to the blood of the prophets the blood of Christ and had filled up the measure of their fathers. Then they were more deservedly punished. For it was not the sin which Cain sinned in killing his brother, nor the sin of those who killed the prophets, that this generation of the Jews which existed in the time of Christ took upon itself; but it was necessary that the patience of God, which was shown toward the nation of the Jews, should be brought to an end by the measures being filled, so that after the many outpourings of the blood of the prophets and of the righteous, Jerusalem and Judea, not desolated earlier, should suffer this afterward in the blood of Christ; and on account of this, God acting magnanimously, so that the scribes and Pharisees, with the people consenting, might receive the blood of the prophets of Christ and — according to the Gospel — of the wise men and scribes, whom they killed and crucified and chastised in their synagogues and persecuted from city to city: so that, with all cast out of Judea, the place, emptied of all the saints, might be made desolate and suffer whatever things they suffered from Vespasian and Titus. These things we have expounded corporeally.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
But if we must also expound these very things morally, we shall say such things in their place. I think that just as Christ came concealed in a body, so that by carnal men, who look at the appearance of His body and do not consider His powers, He was seen as a man, but by spiritual men, who do not attend to the appearance of His body but consider the works of His powers, He is understood to be God — so also is all divine Scripture embodied, but most especially that of the Old Testament. For the spiritual and prophetic sense of Scripture is concealed within the history of the matter set forth, so that all Scripture is understood by ordinary people according to the history, but by the spiritual and perfect according to the spiritual mystery.

Having set down this preface, let us return to the text. For just as, in the prophets themselves when they departed from this life, their bodies indeed were in the tombs, but their souls and spirits were "in the region of the living", so also in the prophetic sayings it must be observed that their narrative according to the simple history is the body, while the spiritual sense and the very inmost truth of the Scriptures is the soul and spirit, which dwells within the simpler narratives according to the history. And the tombs of the prophets we can not inappropriately reckon to be the very letters of the Scriptures and the books, in which the narrative, once placed there, remains as it were a body laid in tombs. Those, therefore, who understand and receive the spiritual things of the Scriptures and their truth concealed within, have in themselves the souls and spirits of the prophets, being themselves made as it were the region of the living prophets. But those who neither grasp nor seek those things, but attend only to the simple narrative and the history of the matter, honor the bodies of the prophets set down in the letters and in the books as in certain tombs: such as were also the Pharisees, who are rightly called Pharisees (that is, THE SEVERED), who severed the spiritual things of the prophets from the corporeal history, as it were driving the soul of the prophets out from the body and slaying the prophecies themselves and making them lifeless, as though they had nothing spiritual. And they are truly hypocrites, building and adorning only the tombs of the prophets which contain the corporeal history — that is, giving zealous study to the very Scriptures and books of the prophets. Not understanding that, in honoring dead bodies (that is, the historical narratives), they seem indeed to act piously concerning the memory of the prophets, but are impious; and by this very thing they wish to defend that they are not associates of those who killed the prophets, yet they are convicted of adding to the crimes of those who killed the prophets and filling up the measure of their iniquity by this very thing — that they do not believe in Christ, whom not the simple histories of the prophets but their spiritual sense proclaims.

But know without doubt that everywhere the cause of the unbelief of the Jews was this: that they did not understand Jesus as the "Christ of God", because they always gave their mind to the corporeal histories, unwilling to believe anything spiritual in them. For example, we introduce for the sake of illustration what is prophesied and said in Zechariah, that as it were "upon an ass and a colt He would enter into Jerusalem and would destroy the "chariots out of Ephraim and the horse out of Jerusalem". If anyone wishes to understand this of Christ according to the history of the letter, it does not fit; for Christ is nowhere expounded to have destroyed out of Ephraim corporeal and perceptible chariots, nor a corporeal horse from a corporeal Jerusalem. But if you see among the heretics the assemblies of falsehood itself coupled together as by a certain yoke and in evil concord among themselves, which the word of truth is wont to destroy, you will see how Christ, the Word of God, destroys the spiritual chariots out of the spiritual Ephraim; for Ephraim is always set as a figure of the heresies, which have separated themselves from the Church of Christ, just as Ephraim from the tribe of Judah. For just as the divine word spiritually "cast into the sea" the horse and rider of the Egyptians, that is, the impious man together with the devil as his rider and yoke-fellow, so also it destroyed the horse from Jerusalem — whoever is subject to the devil as his rider and not to Christ, as are those horses acceptable to Christ, of whom Habakkuk says: "because you will mount upon your horses, and your cavalry is salvation", that is, upon the apostles and the other saints in whom Christ dwells. Therefore we say: "these in chariots" (pointing to Ephraim) "and these on horses" (pointing to the adversaries of Jerusalem), "but we shall be magnified in the name of our God. They are bound and have fallen, but we have risen and are set upright". These bear witness to themselves that they are sons of those who killed the prophets by this very thing, that they fill up the measure of their fathers, adding to the unbelief of those men their unbelief in Jesus, which comes from no other source than that they are occupied with nothing else except the buildings of the prophetic tombs — that is, with diligent attention to the prophetic letters and books only.

For the scribes of the law are one thing — the unhappy ones — but the scribes who are sent by Christ according to the Gospel are another, whose spirit gives life and whose letter does not kill, as does the letter of the law; because those who follow the letter of the law run into unbelief and into empty superstitions, but those who follow the letter of the Gospel (that is, its simple narrative) are saved, since even the simple narrative of the Gospel alone suffices for the simpler sort unto salvation. And if you see the scribes of the law and the Pharisees acting not only against the wise men of the Gospel and those prophesying the things that are Christ's, but even against the scribes of the new testament, you will see how (as far as lies in them) they kill the prophets of Christ and crucify the scribes through the disparagement of their words, and scourge them in their synagogues. Frequently, therefore, it may be heard among the heresies, who are the spiritual Pharisees, how with their tongues, as with certain lashes of their evil speech, they scourge and persecute Christians from city to city. Sometimes indeed even corporeally, but sometimes spiritually, wishing to drive them out as it were from their own city of the law and the prophets and the Gospel and the apostles, and into another and foreign city of some other gospel, they drive them by their lying persuasions as by persecutions. According to which the apostle also said, on account of the false apostles: "I marvel that you are so quickly transferred from the grace of God, who called you, to another gospel, which is not another; unless there are certain persons who trouble you". On account of which there shall come upon them all the just blood, which they pour out by this very thing, that they wish to overthrow the truth of the Scriptures, which is rightly called the blood and life of the Scriptures, because all Scripture, unless it be understood according to the truth, is dead. They pour out, therefore, the truth of the Scriptures as their blood, just as the blood of Abel was poured out.

And not only then did the voice of Abel's blood cry out to God, but also always the truth of the Scriptures, poured out by the impious according to what we have said (beginning from the blood of Christ, that is, from the truth of the Gospel), through all the Scriptures pleads to God against those who wish to overthrow it; and the "blood of the testament", that is, the truth of the prophetic Scriptures, pleads against those who reckoned it unclean and were unwilling to be sanctified in it as in living and sanctifying blood. Thus they pour out also the blood of Zechariah, which is interpreted "the memory of God." For everyone who hastens to destroy the memory of God in those whom he scandalizes seems to pour out the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah, which itself is interpreted THE BLESSING OF GOD. For through the blessing of God we are mindful of God. And if we ought not to leave even the name Abel undiscussed, we say that Abel is interpreted MOURNING. He, therefore, who receives what is written: "blessed are they that mourn", saves Abel; but he who does not receive it pours out the blood of Abel, that is, the truth of saving mourning. Therefore there shall be fulfilled upon him what is written: "woe to you who laugh now, for you shall mourn and weep". Between the temple and the altar the memory of God is slain by the impious. When both the temple of God is corrupted by the wanton, and His altar is defiled through the negligence of sordid prayers. When even someone's prayer becomes unto his own sin, as also is said concerning the prayer of Judas: "and let his prayer become unto his sin".

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
And in the prophetic writings, the historical sense is the body, the spiritual meaning is the soul; the sepulchres are the letter and books themselves of Scripture. They then who attend only to the historical meaning, honour the bodies of the Prophets, and set in the letter as in a sepulchre; and are called Pharisees, i. e. 'cut off,' as it were cutting off the soul of the Prophets from their body.

They fill up the measure of their fathers' sins by their not believing in Christ. And the cause of their unbelief was, that they looked only to the letter and the body, and would understand nothing spiritual in them.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: It is also in your power to cast off the image of the serpent as well. Indeed, Scripture calls the evil man a serpent and a brood of vipers. But if you seek confirmation that we are able to change and to cease being serpents, swine, or dogs, let us turn to the words of the Apostle, that the transformation depends on us. … If you were a raging beast and heard the Word, which will tame and domesticate you and which at Its own discretion will turn you into a man — you will never again hear said of you: serpent, brood of vipers. Because, if it were impossible to be rid of these serpents, the serpents residing in the soul on account of its wickedness, then the Savior (or John) would not have said: "Bring forth then fruits worthy of repentance!" Having turned, you will no longer be serpents, broods of vipers.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: Or the Scribes who are sent by Christ, are Scribes according to the Gospel, whom the spirit quickens and the letter does not kill, as did the letter of the Law, which whoso followed ran into vain superstitions. The simple words of the Gospel are sufficient for salvation. But the Scribes of the Law do yet scourge the Scribes of the New Testament, by detracting from them in their synagogues; and the heretics also, who are spiritual Pharisees, with their tongues murder the Christians, and persecute them from city to city, sometimes in the body, sometimes also in the spirit, seeking to drive them from their own city of the Law, the Prophets, and the Gospel, into another Gospel.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
A tradition has come down to us, that there was one place in the temple in which virgins were allowed to worship God, married women being forbidden to stand there. And Mary, after the Saviour's birth, going into the temple, stood to pray in this place of the virgins. And when they who knew that she had borne a Son were hindering her, Zacharias said, that forasmuch as she was still a virgin, she was worthy of the place of the virgins. Whereupon, as though he manifestly were contravening the Law, he was slain there between the temple and the altar by the men of that generation; and thus this word of Christ is true which He spake to those who were standing there, whom ye slew.

Zacharias is interpreted 'The memory of God.' Whosoever then hastes to obliterate the memory of God, seems to those to whom he gives offence to shed the blood of Zacharias the son of Barachias. For it is by the blessing of God that we retain the memory of God. Also the memory of God is slain by the wicked, when the Temple of God is polluted by the lustful, and His altar defiled by the carelessness of prayers. Abel is interpreted 'mourning.' He then who does not receive that, Blessed are they that mourn, sheds the blood of Abel, that is, puts away the truth of wholesome mourning. Some also shed, as it were, the blood of the Scriptures by putting aside their truth, for all Scripture, if it is not understood according to its truth, is dead.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: He calls them children of Jerusalem, just as we call each generation of citizens the sons of the preceding generation. And He says, How often, though it is well known that once only did He teach the Jews in the body, because Christ was ever present in Moses, and in the Prophets, and in the Angels, ministering to human salvation in every generation. Whosoever shall not have been gathered in by Him shall be judged, as though he had refused to be gathered in.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: But I think that here too the meaning of that hen is latently held, through whom the purification of the sinner is effected, concerning which it is written: "How often would I have gathered thy children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and thou wouldest not!"

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets, and stone those who are sent to you, how often have I wished to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not? behold, now your house shall be left to you desolate. For I say to you, that from now on you shall not see me until you say: blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.

It is worth inquiring how the Savior, speaking before hearers among whom were scribes and Pharisees who prided themselves on knowing carefully the things of the law and the prophets, on what ground he said that Jerusalem had killed the prophets and had stoned those sent to her, since no such account is much prophesied in the ancient scriptures that were read in their synagogues. We do read that Jeremiah was cast into a pit of mud, yet not that he was killed in Jerusalem. But neither of Isaiah nor of Ezekiel nor of any of the prophets do we read that he suffered any such thing, so far as my memory suggests. But searching in the second book of Chronicles, where many things are written about the famous prophets, I find that Asa, angered at Hanani the prophet who rebuked him, did indeed put him in prison, yet did nothing more to him. And Ahab too ordered Micaiah, who prophesied against him, to go into the prison house and to eat the bread of tribulation, yet did not kill him. But we read of one who was stoned, "Azariah the son of Jehoiada the priest," who was rebuking the people. Therefore we do not find, beyond what I have said, that in Jerusalem prophets were killed, or that those sent to Jerusalem were stoned.

For this reason it must be considered whether perhaps it is necessary to demonstrate the word of Christ from the more secret books which are current among the Jews — and not only the word of Christ but also of his disciples, of Stephen the first martyr and of Paul the apostle. For Stephen speaks thus: "O stiff-necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, you have always resisted the Holy Spirit, as your fathers did, so also you. For which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they killed those who announced the coming of the Just One, of whom you have now become the betrayers and murderers"; and after this: "they drove him outside the city, and they stoned Stephen crying out and saying." And Paul, in the first letter to the Thessalonians, says such things concerning the killing of the prophets: "you became imitators of the churches of God which are in Judea in Christ Jesus, since you too suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews, who both killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and persecuted us, and do not please God." And to the Hebrews thus: "they were stoned, they were sawn in two, they were tempted, they died by the sword, they went about in sheepskins, in goatskins, being in want, distressed, afflicted with sufferings — of whom the world was not worthy — wandering in deserts and in mountains and caves and holes of the earth." It is reported, then, in the scriptures that are not manifest, that Isaiah was sawn in two, and Zechariah killed, and Ezekiel. And I suppose that Elijah, who wandered in the desert and in the mountains, is the one who went about in sheepskins and goatskins. But suppose someone rejects the letter to the Hebrews as not being Paul's, and likewise casts away the secret book of Isaiah: yet what will he do with the words of Stephen, or of Paul to the Thessalonians, brought forward about the prophets killed, or with those of our Lord himself? Or how will he reject that which Paul brought forward to Timothy, saying: "as Jannes and Jambres resisted Moses, so these also resist the truth"? For we do not know in the canonical books the account of Jannes and Jambres resisting Moses. And if he also looks at what is set down in the first letter to the Corinthians, "what eye has not seen nor ear heard," can anyone possibly reject all these things?

All these things we have said in examining the passage, not being ignorant that many of the secret writings have been fabricated by the impious and by those who speak "iniquity on high." And the followers of Hypythianus use certain fabricated writings, and others those of Basilides. It is necessary, therefore, to consider carefully, so that we neither accept all the secret writings that are circulated in the name of the saints — on account of the Jews, who perhaps have fabricated certain things to the destruction of the truth of our scriptures, establishing false doctrines — nor reject all that pertain to the demonstration of our scriptures. It belongs, then, to a great man to hear and fulfill what has been said: "test all things, hold fast what is good." Yet on account of those who cannot, like money-changers, discern among words whether they are to be held true or false, and who cannot keep themselves carefully, so as to hold what is true with them but "abstain from every evil appearance," no one ought to use, for the confirmation of doctrines, books that are outside the canonical scriptures. Nevertheless, if anyone accepts the letter to the Hebrews as Paul's, he will say that we ought not refer plurals altogether to many. For not many were sawn in two, but Isaiah alone; nor were many stoned except Azariah only, the son of Jehoiada; nor was anyone killed by the sword except Zechariah the son of Barachiah; so too in sheepskins and in goatskin, Elijah, and other like cases. And further let us inquire into what is written in Luke, the Lord saying: "because it cannot be that a prophet perish outside Jerusalem." If, then, "it cannot be that a prophet perish outside Jerusalem," that is, be killed, you will ask whether after the destruction of Jerusalem there is now no prophet, lest perhaps the one who is killed "outside Jerusalem" should, being a prophet, prove the word of Christ false. But if the scriptures compel us — on account of Agabus and the daughters of Philip the evangelist (not on account of the false prophets of Phrygia) — let us inquire whether perhaps every righteous person is in Jerusalem and not "outside Jerusalem," since "it cannot be" that the one who is outside Jerusalem be afflicted with sufferings for the sake of the word.

But how Jerusalem killed the prophets must be considered. And I judge that, as people are accustomed to say in common speech — the city cried out, as if it were said, those who are in the city; likewise, the city went out to meet him, that is, those who are in the city — so: Jerusalem killed the prophets, that is, those who were in Jerusalem, on whose account it was said that Jerusalem killed the prophets. And if the citizens are put for the city, again a question arises: who are to be called the children of Jerusalem, concerning whom it was said: how often have I wished to gather your children? But we say that the successors of the citizens are always called the children of those who preceded them. But that Jerusalem which is free from the servitude of sin, which is above in its manner of life, "which is our mother," does not kill the prophets nor stone those who are sent to her. It is another matter that, after the likeness of that Jerusalem which killed and stoned the prophets, frequently there are certain persons set up in this Jerusalem, unskilled and not fearing God, who (as far as in them lies) kill and stone, with words uttered without judgment, men advanced in word and in life — men who indeed do not abandon the canon of the churches, but on account of the profundity of their doctrines are held suspect by those who are accustomed to say certain novel things and do not attend to the "sound word" of our Lord Jesus Christ.

The Lord, therefore, says to Jerusalem the killer and stoner of the prophets: how often have I wished to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not? How is it that here the Lord Jesus, as one who often wished to gather the Jews but did not gather them on account of the obstinacy of those unwilling to believe, says thus: how often have I wished, when it is plain that he taught the Jews in the body only once? But not only in his presence, but also substantially, Christ was always present both in Moses and in the prophets, and still more in the angels ministering to human salvation through the individual generations; and thus is fulfilled what he says: how often have I wished. For through the individual generations he always wished and hastened to accomplish the will of the Father in them, and though not established in the body, as now at the end of the ages, yet he always hastened to gather the children of Jerusalem. For the very words of him wishing to gather the children of Jerusalem are found in the law and in the prophets, and of him it is written: "spreading out his wings he received them, and took them up upon his shoulders"; and it is the daily work of Christ to gather the children of Jerusalem (concerning whom many things are said both in Isaiah and in the rest of the prophets), and daily the Son of God gathers the scattered children of God, as a hen her chicks under her wings. But if anyone has not been gathered by him, he will be judged as one who was unwilling to be gathered by him. "For the Son of Man came to seek what had perished, and to save," and he died "not for the nation alone, but that he might gather into one the scattered children of God." And to the Jews indeed (who were the children of that Jerusalem which was below) he threatened, as they were unwilling to be gathered under his wings, saying: behold, now your house shall be left to you desolate. And always to those who are unwilling to be gathered under his wings Christ seems to threaten and to say: behold, now your house shall be left to you desolate, that is, your soul and body. For not only the body, but also the soul of those who sin, is left desolate, and (as in a desert) foxes make lairs in them, and serpents, the brood of vipers, their resting-places.

But he says to those unwilling to be gathered to him: that you shall not see me from now on until you say: blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. And not even then did the Jews see Christ, for he was not seen by them rising from the dead as before, but by judgment and grace only by the fathers who were worthy. And until, understanding their own desolation, they say in penitence: blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, they will not see the Son of God, nor will they see his word, nor will they consider the beauty of the wisdom of God. But even if any of us should wish to be gathered under the wings of Christ, yet by evil works should refuse to be gathered under his wings, he will now not see the word of God — especially from that time from which he flees the one who gathers him, day by day, by his action rather than by his body. And so long he will not see the beauty of the word, that is, Christ himself, until, converted and repentant from his evil purpose, he says: blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord. For then the blessed word of God and the blessed wisdom of God, coming, comes in the name of God and of the Father upon the heart of man, when someone has been converted to him.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: In like manner to all such as would not be gathered under His wings Christ speaks this threat; Behold, your house is left unto you desolate; i. e. your soul and your body. But if any one of you will not be gathered under the wings of Christ, from the very time when he shall have refused to be so gathered, (by a mental rather than a bodily act,) he shall no more see the beauty of the word, till repenting of his evil purpose he shall say, Blessed is He that cometh in the name of the Lord. And the word of the Lord then comes with a blessing upon a man's heart, when one is turned to God.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: Christ, when He had foretold all that should come upon Jerusalem, went forth out of the temple, He, who while He was in it, had upheld the temple that it should not fall. And so each man, being the temple of God by reason of the Spirit of God dwelling in him, is himself the cause of his being deserted, that Christ should depart from him. It is worthy of note how they show Him the buildings of the temple, as though He had never seen them. We reply, that when Christ had foretold the destruction that should come upon the temple, His disciples were amazed at the thought that so magnificent buildings should be utterly ruined, and therefore they show them to Him to move Him to pity, that He would not do what He had threatened. And because the constitution of human nature is wonderful, being made the temple of God, the disciples and the rest of the saints confessing the wonderful working of God in respect of the forming of men, intercede before the face of Christ, that He would not forsake the human race for their sins.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
And Jesus went out from the temple and was departing; and his disciples came to him, to show him the buildings of the temple. But Jesus answering said to them: do you see all these things? amen I say to you, there shall not be left here a stone upon a stone that shall not be destroyed.

After Christ had foretold all the things that were to come upon Jerusalem, he went out from the temple — he who had preserved the temple, lest it fall, so long as he was in it. For as long as the Word was among the Jews, not taking the kingdom of God away from them, so long it stood, and the affairs of the Jews were unharmed. But after, according to his own word which he had spoken: "the kingdom of God shall be taken away from you and shall be given to a nation producing its own fruit", he took away the kingdom of God and gave it to the Gentiles, then both Jesus and the kingdom of God came to be among the Gentiles. Hence now neither Jesus nor the kingdom of God is held among the Jews, because they have been left "like a tabernacle in a vineyard, and like a hut in a cucumber-field, and like a city that is besieged", on account of the crime which they committed against Christ.

And each one who receives the word of God is a temple of God, so that it may rightly be said to him: "Do you not know that you are the temple of God and that the Spirit of God dwells in you?" Each one therefore, since he is a holy temple of God because of the Spirit of God dwelling within him, if he himself sins, becomes the cause of his own desertion, so that Christ goes out from him, so that he who had before been a temple of the Son of God is thereafter a deserted house, so that there is not left in him a stone upon a stone — out of all the doctrines and edifications of a good life — that is not destroyed. On account of which, calling to mind the history of the desertion of Jerusalem, we ought to look out for ourselves, that Christ not go out from the temple (which is made up of us), that the buildings of our temple may be unharmed, adorned with stones and gifts, so that those who see the buildings that are in us may say in wonder: "see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings". But this is worthy to be examined thoroughly, how, as far as the text goes, the disciples speak thus to Jesus, and show him the buildings of stones, as though someone who had never seen the temple itself but had come from elsewhere as a stranger arriving for the first time. To this it must be answered thus: that when above, prophesying its coming ruin, Christ had thus threatened its desertion: "behold, now your house shall be left to you deserted", the disciples, hearing it, marveled that such and so great a building of the temple was to be reduced to nothing. Therefore they say to Jesus (as another evangelist says more plainly): "master, do you see what kind of stones and what kind of buildings", namely so that they might bend him to mercy for that place, that he not do what he had threatened to do.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: And let these things be understood in a bodily sense; but morally in this way: since the marvelous construction of human nature has been made — namely, the temple of God and of his Word — the disciples and the other saints (not only then, but even now confessing the wondrous works of God toward the human creature) intercede before the sight of Christ and appeal to Christ, that he may not abandon the human race on account of their sins, but rather that his wondrous works may move him to indulgence more than their iniquities move him to wrath. Otherwise: just as that temple was not demolished all at once but little by little as time went on, so also every man who takes into himself the Word of God is a temple; and if indeed after sin he has not fallen away wholly from the Word of God, but still preserves in part the traces of faith and of the religious keeping of God's commandments within himself, he is a temple in part destroyed and in part still standing. But whoever, after he has sinned, takes no care of himself, but is ever running away from faith and from the life which is according to the Gospel, is diminished little by little, until he wholly withdraws "from the living God" — this man is a temple in which there shall not be left a stone of doctrine upon a stone of God's commandments that shall not be thrown down. We, therefore, ought to look out for ourselves, that the whole building of piety may remain intact within us, so that, both adorned with the stones of saving doctrines and decorated with the gifts of good works, we may take into ourselves the power and glory of God, and Christ, who is the Word and Wisdom of God.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: And someone introduces a third exposition of this kind: that the temple of God was built by a composition of words that carry meaning, namely the whole Scripture of the Old Testament constructed according to its history. Those who constructed it — Moses or the prophets — by the setting-together of letters and the ordering of sayings, built it to be admired by all for the beauty of its stones, that is, of the choice sayings and of the sense-meanings to be praised as gifts. This the disciples point out to Jesus, taking up all the Scriptures; and to them Christ replies, saying that this bodily and first building is to be destroyed by the Word, so that a more divine and more mysterious temple of another Scripture may be built. That the Scripture is a temple was expounded by someone before us. And since the Antichrist — "he who opposes and exalts himself above everything that is called God", who sits in the temple of God — is the false word that is held in the Scriptures — which counterfeits the truth by bringing forward, out of the Scriptures, testimonies of impious teachings, when men are unwilling to be won over from any other source; and this very thing is "that which opposes", and it sits both upon the seat of the Scriptures and upon their building, "displaying itself as though it were God". And one may always see the words of the heresies, as Antichrists, sitting in the temple of the Scriptures and wishing, out of those very Scriptures, to win over those who hear them, as though each one of these were itself God the Word in the Scriptures.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: Every man also, who, by taking into him the word of God, is become a temple, if after sinning he yet retains in part the traces of faith and religion, his temple is in part destroyed, and in part standing. But he who after sin has no regard for himself is gradually alienated, until he has altogether forsaken the living God, and so one stone is not left upon another of God's commandments, which he has not thrown down.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
I think Mount Olivet to be a mystery of the Church out of the Gentiles.

For the husbandman dwelling on Mount Olivet is the word of God confirmed in the Church, that is, Christ, who ever grafts the branches of the wild olive on the good olive tree of the Fathers. They who have confidence before Christ, seek to learn the sign of the coming of Christ, and of the consummation of this world. And the coming of the Word into the soul is of two sorts. The first is that foolish preaching concerning Christ, when we preach that Christ was born and crucified; the second its coming in perfect men, concerning which it is said, We speak wisdom among them that are perfect; (1 Cor. 2:6.) and to this second coming is added the end of the world in the perfect man to whom the world is crucified.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
But as he was sitting upon the Mount of Olives, his disciples came to him privately, saying: tell us, when shall these things be, and what shall be the sign of your coming and of the consummation of the age.

"When Jesus had gone out of the temple", after he had spoken concerning it, he came to the Mount of Olives and there sat with his disciples. But I think that the Mount of Olives is a mystery of the Church which is from the Gentiles, in which olive trees have been planted, each one of which can say: "but I am like a fruitful olive tree in the house of God". And perhaps too on this Mount of Olives the roots of the good olive tree are present, but the branches of the wild olive have been grafted in in the place of the branches which "were cut off through unbelief". And the husbandman residing on the Mount of Olives is the Word of God confirmed in the Church, Christ, who is ever grafting the branches of the wild olive into the good olive tree of the fathers, of Moses and of the rest of the prophets, so that, receiving richness from the holy prophets (through this, that they carefully understand their meaning, and receive also the Christ who is prophesied by them), they may offer abundant and richer fruit—than, that is to say, the former olives, which because of the curse that was in the law have been shaken down, so that they can no longer be of use.

After this it must be considered that, of the disciples approaching Jesus, some indeed approach him privately, having in this very thing greater confidence with him as those of his household (as when they questioned him about the solving of the parables), but others questioned him not privately but in common. Observe further the difference between these, that at times indeed the Pharisees approach, whether tempting him or questioning him in whatever manner, but at other times others desiring to learn—yet these never approach privately out of the multitude. And perhaps even now those who have taken up a distinguished life and on account of this have confidence before Christ, having something more than those who from the common faith approach Jesus, say to him: tell us, when shall these things be? these things—which? that which he said: "there shall not stand here one stone upon a stone which shall not be destroyed". And they wish to learn not only this, but also the sign of the coming of Christ and of the consummation of the age; and two things they ask of him, the sign of his coming and of the consummation of the age. Therefore the coming of the Son of God and the consummation of the age is indeed believed among many, but especially among those who pursue a more refined life.

It is possible also in another way to see a twofold coming of Christ, that is, the coming of the Word into the soul. First indeed the untrained and those then beginning to know Christ, because they cannot see the brightness of his beauty, say: "we saw him, and he had no form nor comeliness, but his appearance was without honor". Now the unhonored appearance of the Word is the foolish preaching about Christ, when we preach Christ born and crucified. But the second coming is the coming of Christ among perfect men, concerning whom the steward of his word says: "but we speak wisdom among the perfect". And these perfect ones have become lovers of his beauty and beseech the Word, that he gird upon himself his rational sword and set it about the mystery of the fleshly nativity, which is called mystically the thigh. For disciples of this kind praise the beauty and comeliness of the Word, and to this second coming is joined the consummation of the age in the man coming to perfection and saying: "but far be it from me to glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom the world is crucified to me and I to the world". For if the world has been crucified to the just, to whom "the world has been crucified", then the consummation of the world has also been made for them. Necessarily, therefore, those who have the confidence of approaching privately to Christ wish to learn the sign of the coming of Christ and of the consummation of the age, so that, being benefited by this—that they have learned the coming of Christ and the consummation—they may show themselves worthy to see his second coming and the consummation of the age according to what we have handed down.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
And Jesus answering said to them: See that no one seduces you. For many will come in my name saying that I am the Christ, and they will seduce many (24, 4. 5).

Those who understand simply suppose that these words signify only this: that many were going to come asserting themselves to be Christs, having in themselves also certain wonder-working powers and words by which they might provoke to belief many who had shown themselves worthy of seduction. But John in his epistle says: "and as you have heard that Antichrist is coming, now many Antichrists have arisen; whence we know that it is the last hour". By these words he teaches that every word which is foreign to the truth and asserts itself to be the word of God is Antichrist; for it is thus possible to understand what he says: "and now many Antichrists have arisen", since there is one thing that is true. But as the record of the readings makes plain, there were not many men in the time of the apostles who said that they were Christs, unless perhaps Dositheus the Samaritan — whence they are also called Dositheans — and Simon, of whom the Acts report, who proclaimed himself to be the great power of God. Besides these, there were none either before or afterward, so far as my knowledge goes.

But every discourse which professes an exposition of the Scriptures and faith in them, yet does not have the truth, is rightly to be understood to be Antichrist, coming in the name of Christ and saying that I am the Christ, lying and by no means able to display in itself the form of truth. And since to those who examine the words of Scripture, in order to find its meaning, there frequently occur certain interpretations as if true when they are not true, and sometimes they are drawn also by other plausible, specious discourses, so that it is not easy to find which is the true meaning before against the lying estimations the truer and firmer meaning has been found — for this reason I think that Christ, to the question of his disciples saying: "when shall these things be? and what is the sign of your coming and of the consummation of the age?" answered thus: See that no one seduces you. For many will come in my name saying: I am the Christ, and they will seduce many. For truly he who fulfills that commandment which says: "be prudent money-changers", and that which says: "prove all things, hold fast what is good; abstain yourselves from every evil appearance", will see many being seduced by false interpretations and words professing themselves to be Christ the word of God. And would that only those who are outside the Church were seduced: it would be easy to guard against the seduction. But now those very people who profess themselves to be churchmen are deceived and seduced about various necessary chapters, as their very dissension is a testimony, since even those who are within are seduced.

But consequently, just as it is wont to be among those wandering these bodily roads that there is a difference of error, and some indeed even go against the very public road that is sought, wandering, while others turn aside a little something from the straight path so that they may be recalled, and there are many differences among those who wander — in this manner we see also those who stray from the truth. And the Marcionites indeed and Basilides, and the Valentinians and the Apellians and the Ophites wander much from the proposed way, since they hold opinions wholly contrary to the truth. But some do not indeed dissent about the public and manifest chapters — for instance, about the one God who gave the Law and the Gospel, or about Christ Jesus the firstborn of every creature, who at the end of the age according to the preachings of the prophets came into the world and took upon himself the true nature of human flesh, so that he even underwent birth from a virgin, and took upon himself the death of the cross and rose from the dead and deified the human nature which he had taken up. Furthermore also about the Holy Spirit, that he himself was the one in the patriarchs and prophets who afterward was given in the apostles, and about the resurrection of the dead as the Gospel teaches they most certainly believe, and all things whatsoever are handed down in the churches. But about other things not few, yet slight, they propose new dogmas, and they too indeed are among those who are seduced by false interpretations and words coming in the name of Christ, who is the word and the truth. And it is an evil indeed to find someone erring according to the conduct of life, but I think it is much worse to go astray in dogmas and not to hold opinions according to the truest rule of the Scriptures. For if for moral sins we are to be punished, still more those sinning through false dogmas. For if a good conduct of morals sufficed for men unto salvation, how is it that among the Gentiles many philosophers, or among the heretics many living continently, are by no means saved, as though the falsity of their dogma obscured and defiled their conduct?

But I think that the discourse, wishing to show a general cleanness which is not only in acts but also in knowledge, says in the twenty-third Psalm: who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord, or who shall stand in his holy place? he that is innocent in hands and pure in heart, and in the Proverbs: who shall boast that he has a chaste heart? or who shall be confident that he is clean from sins? I therefore think that the one clean in heart and chaste in heart is no other than he who possesses a heart clean and chaste from every false dogma; so also I reckon him to be innocent in hands and clean from sins who is irreproachable in the acts of his life. And it must be known that (as regards the truth) it is impossible for anyone to be innocent in hands and clean from sins without being pure in heart and chaste from false dogmas; just as, on the contrary, it is impossible to be clean indeed and chaste in heart from false dogmas without being innocent in "hands" and clean from sins. For these follow one another mutually and are not separated from each other: a discourse clean in the soul and a life irreproachable. But we have treated this chapter more abundantly, teaching ourselves according to what has seemed good to us in the passage, that we may keep ourselves from every error of false dogmas, whether about the manifest and principal chapters or about those which seem lesser, that we may hear him who said: "you shall not turn aside to the right or to the left", from him who said: "I am the way", and that we may not be seduced, but may keep watch lest any of those deceive us who come in the name of Christ saying: I am the Christ, I am the truth and wisdom and the true light.

But I think that not only is discourse Christ and feigned discourse Antichrist, truth Christ and feigned truth Antichrist, wisdom Christ and feigned wisdom Antichrist (deceiving the lovers of the wisdom of God and of truth, all of which pertain to the account of faith), but also in these virtues by which we live according to God, we find that all the virtues are Christ and all the feigned virtues Antichrist, since all the kinds of good, whatsoever Christ has in himself in truth for the edification of men, all of these the devil has in himself in appearance for the seduction of the saints. For thus Christ is righteousness, yet "there are" frequently "ways of a man which seem to be righteous, but the last of them look down into the depth of hell". When therefore something seems to be righteousness, while it is not true righteousness, such righteousness is Antichrist against Christ who is righteousness. I think also that there is a chastity that is Antichrist, which is among the heretics sending men into error, that they may not understand the ecclesiastical chastity which is Christ. So also there is a mercy that is Antichrist against the mercy which is Christ, in those who give alms, but not for the sake of the righteousness of God. There is also a patience that is Antichrist in those who indeed seem to suffer for Christianity and "striving even to the shedding of blood", that is, lest they seem to deny Christianity; yet in that very shedding of their blood they "speak iniquity on high", and set "their mouth in heaven". There is also a power that is Antichrist seducing the ignorant, since many are going to say to Christ in that day: "Lord, in your name we cast out demons, and did many powerful works", to whom he will answer: "depart from me, all you who work iniquity, I never knew you". For if Christ never knew them, yet they boast that they did powerful works in the name of Christ, those powers were not from Christ who had not known them, but from him who "transfigures himself" not only "into an angel of light" but even into Christ himself. There is need therefore for us of God as helper and of Christ himself living in us, that with our eyes opened we may see, lest anyone seduce us — either a discourse or a power, whether from within or from without — promising itself to be Christ, when it is his enemy and the enemy of his other virtues.

Consider also this, that many come in nothing else but in my name; for Antichrist takes up only the name of Christ, and neither does the works nor teaches the words of his truth nor displays his wisdom in himself. And just as (according to some) Barabbas too was called Jesus, but was a robber having nothing of Jesus except the name, so I reckon there are many Christs, but in name only. Note, however, that nowhere in the Scriptures is the Lord found using this very expression and saying: I am the Christ, so that he might say nothing similar to the many who were going to come in his name and to say: I am the Christ. For there sufficed for him, unto the faith of believers (that he himself is the Christ), the works of God, which Christ alone could do, and the discourse which he taught and the power, above a thousand voices crying out: I am the Christ. And thus he never openly said: I am, but he said it through works and through the teaching of piety, so that he himself says to Peter, as to one who had never heard it from him but had learned from the Father, that he himself was "the Christ, the Son of the living God": "blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because not flesh and blood revealed it to you, but my Father who is in the heavens". For if he himself, while set in the body, had openly said to him: I am the Christ, flesh would have seemed to have revealed it to him, and not the Father only. Therefore it suffices for the seduction of the Antichrists this alone which they say: I am the Christ, which Christ is never read to have said, and there are many who are seduced; "for wide is the gate and spacious the way that leads to perdition, and many enter through it"; but few are those who find that way "which leads to life".

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: They that are deceived are many, because wide is the gate that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat. (Mat. 7:13.) This one thing is enough to detect the Antichrists and seducers that they shall say, I am Christ, which Christ Himself is no where read to have said: for the works of God, and the word which He taught, and His power, were enough to produce belief that He is Christ. For every discourse which professes to expound Scripture faithfully, and has not the truth, is Antichrist. For the truth is Christ, that which feigns itself to be the truth is Antichrist. So also all virtues are Christ, all that feigns itself to be virtue is Antichrist; for Christ has in Himself in truth all manner of good for the edification of men, but the devil has forged resemblances of the same for the deceiving of the saints. We have need therefore of God to help us, that none deceive us, neither word nor power. It is a bad thing to find any one erring in his course of life; but I esteem it much worse not to think according to the most true rule of Scripture.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
To hear the shouts raised in the battles, is to hear wars; to hear rumours of wars, is to hear accounts of wars waged afar off.

This must come to pass before we can see the perfection of that wisdom which is in Christ; but not yet shall be that end which we seek, for a peaceful end is far from those men.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
But you shall hear battles and rumors of battles; see that you are not terrified, for these things must happen, but the end is not yet.

Luke, however, puts it this way: "when you hear of battles and seditions, do not be terrified; for these things must first happen, but the end is not at once". In these words he sets forth two things, one thus: you shall hear battles, the other: rumors of battles. And first let us see, according to the simple tradition, in the way that many understand it, how rumors of battles differ from battles. Suppose for me that battles exist where cities rise up against cities or nations against nations, so that the one may carry off the other's property or the stronger may kill the strong. What, then, do rumors of battles signify after battles? Especially since it is not said: you shall see battles and hear about battles, but on both sides he set you shall hear; that is, both you shall hear battles and you shall hear rumors of battles. And let us suppose that to hear battles is when the sons of peace keep their eyes clean from battles, so that they may not see wicked things; and (since they cannot look upon labors and pains) they hear about battles, what sort of city fights against what sort of city or what sort of nation is stormed by what sort of nation. But what else, besides this, will it be to hear battles and to hear rumors of battles? See, then, whether you can (I speak with regard to the simplicity of the word) give such a distinction: it is not one and the same thing to hear from far off, placed away from a battle, that a battle is happening, and to be beside the battle and to hear the very voices of those fighting. Each, therefore, has its own signification. And perhaps he indeed who hears the very voices which are made in battles, hears battles; but he who hears about battles waged far off, hears rumors of battles. For he does not hear the battles themselves. But since the words are ambiguous, someone may say the reverse, that he who is indeed far from the battles hears about them; while he who is beside the battles hears the rumors of the battles themselves. In both ways, therefore, there seems to be some understanding of the difference.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
Rise now to the moral and spiritual understanding, if in any way you can find some interpretation worthy of the eminence of Christ's knowledge and of the subtlety of the evangelists, so that you may not lay aside the dignity of evangelical wisdom. See therefore whether, recalling those things which were set forth above concerning what he says: many will come in my name saying: I am Christ, and they will lead many astray, we can, according to their sequence, interpret these things also. Everyone therefore who is perfect and sees in his own soul the glorious coming of the Word — which corrupts and consummates the world and crucifies it to the just man, that all worldly things may die to him — and who has senses trained for grasping, must, as he seeks and examines, run into many battles of doctrines. He will hear also many professing the truth and diverse traditions concerning it, so that, like a good soldier of the Word, he may remain invulnerable in soul against all those professing the truth but not seeing it nor manifesting it, but rather pronouncing things contrary to the truth as though they were the truth; and he may be made worthy to receive into his soul the glorious coming of Christ, according to that whereby he is God the Word, which was in the beginning with God, which is wont to come to those who, after they have known Christ according to the flesh and have received the Word which was made flesh, ascend so far beyond the many that they can grasp not just any sort of glory, but glory as of the only-begotten from the Father.

And perhaps the Word of God appears in diverse glories, according to the power of each soul that sees, according to the capacity that each single soul has offered. To the one, therefore, who is perfect and has arrived at the consummation of the age, insofar as it depends on him, the Word appears such that whoever has seen him may say: "we have seen his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth". Therefore, if anyone is to be held worthy to receive such a Word and to see it, he must, before a vision of the word of this kind, hear in his soul battles; but through others, who assert as though it were truth whatever has seemed so to them, rumors of battles. And rightly, as his disciples were advancing toward perfection, after the Savior had spoken these things about battles, he added further: see, and did not say: hear, urging them to be watchful, so that they might be able to see with the eyes of the soul (after they have heard battles and rumors of battles) the nature of each of the things that are heard, and, seeing it, not be terrified: because such intelligible battles are wont to arise for righteous men amid diverse persuasions, and to disturb and shake their souls into doubting, lest perhaps those things be true which seem to be probable while they are false, or at any rate into believing them completely as though they were true.

As many, therefore, as set out toward the perfection which is in Christ and toward the manner of life of the heavenly church, when they have heard the battles of the heresies, which do battle against the true faith and against one another in turn, and when they have heard the rumors of battles of "philosophy and vain seduction according to the tradition of men, according to the elements of this world, and not according to Christ", exercising themselves in the things that are said, seek and ponder the commandment of Christ who says: see, and they do indeed see the things that are said, but seeing lies dressed up with the appearance of truth, they are not led astray, but they hope, without any wound from such battles, to see the glorious coming of Christ, who is the word; especially if, hearing according to Christ's commandment of battles and rumors of battles, they suffer no disturbance of soul, but, protected under the peace of God which guards the "hearts and minds" of the worthy, they are not terrified. But if anyone, hearing of battles and rumors of battles, according to what we have expounded, is not attentive to see the things that are said in their various appearances of truth, and because he was not attentive to see is terrified, he will not only be deceived by the many who come in the name of Christ and say: I am Christ, but he will even be slain by swords of this kind, receiving incurable wounds — of which swords it is said: "swords do wound", whose wounds "the tongues of the wise" are wont to heal. But these who are disturbed and, because they do not look out for themselves, fall into a battle of this kind, are those who are wounded in the valley of Zion. and they die, of whom Scripture says: "your wounded are not wounded by the sword, nor are your dead dead in battle", concerning whom it is fitting for us now only to give this indication.

But it is not for just any man to prepare himself to hear of wars and rumors of wars, so that hearing he may see and not be terrified, but for the man perfected in Christ, living indeed in the flesh yet not warring according to the flesh, whose weapons of warfare are not carnal but mighty toward God and able to destroy strongholds and the reasonings of those who exalt themselves against the knowledge of God. For, according to Solomon, the many "fortified cities" of the heresies, fortified by the persuasion of words, "a wise man ascended," and ascending he "destroyed the fortification in which the impious trusted." Paul destroyed it, who had been prepared "for the destruction of fortified cities" set against the truth. Such a man, after he has heard of wars and rumors of wars, seeing and, as one wise, ascending upon the "fortified cities" and destroying the "fortifications in which the impious trusted," praising God and giving thanks to God (from whom he learned to fight such wars, and to keep the commandment which says: "sanctify war"), cries out and says: "Blessed be the Lord God, who teaches my hands for war, and my fingers for battle; my mercy and my refuge." And because of wars of this kind it is said of David by the wife of Nabal: "My lord will fight the wars of the Lord." And I think that these wars, which are read of in the Scriptures, are also mysteries of such battles; and that the destruction of those who fight against the congregation of the truth is likewise a mystery — especially those things which are read in the book of Joshua the son of Nun concerning the destructions of cities, and they are mysteries of all the congregations of the adversary powers.

Hearing, therefore, of wars and rumors of such wars, let us attend to what he says: see that you be not terrified. And we ought to know that it is necessary for these things to happen to one awaiting the coming of the Word, that he may hear wars and rumors of wars, but not immediately, as soon as he has heard, will the end be. For this reason every man who wishes to be saved must await the end, since "whoever shall persevere unto the end, this one shall be saved". According to Luke, however, if we hear of "wars and insurrections", let us not be troubled — the wars being those that arise from "knowledge falsely so named" and from the wisdom of "the princes of this world", and the insurrections being those of people who do not agree among themselves in the assembly of the church. For we plainly hear differing opinions about various matters (especially we who wish to advance toward that perfection which is in Christ) — not only wars outside the church, but also insurrections within the church itself. From all these things the disciples of the apostles were strangers, of all of whom, as is written in the Acts of the Apostles, "there was one heart and one soul"; for they had been confirmed "in the same mind and in the same knowledge". Yet let us, even if we hear of wars of this kind and insurrections of this sort, not be terrified. For "these things must first come to pass", before we behold the perfection of the wisdom which is in Christ; "but the end" which we seek "shall not be at once". For we must be made stable and confirmed in peace, so that we may be without terror and not be troubled by insurrections, so that after these things we may be able to attain that end which lies not in the hearing of wars nor in the insurrections themselves; for the peaceful end is far removed from all these things.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote: Or otherwise; As the body sickens before the death of the man, so it must needs be that before the consummation of this world the earth should be shaken, as though it were palsied, with frequent earthquakes, the air should gather a deadly quality and become pestilential, and that the vital energy of the soil should fail, and its fruits wither. And by consequence of this scarcity, men are stirred up to robbery and war. But because war and strife arise sometimes from covctousness, and sometimes from desire of power and empty glory, of these which shall happen before the end of the world a yet deeper cause shall be assignable. For as Christ's coming brought through His divine power peace to divers nations, so it shall be on the other hand, that when iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold, and God and His Christ shall desert them; wars shall be again when actions which beget wars are not hindered by holiness; and hostile powers when they are not restrained by the Saints and by Christ shall work unchecked in the hearts of men, stirring up nation against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. But if, as some will have it, famine and pestilence are from the Angels of Satan, these shall then gather might from opposite powers, when the salt of the earth, and the lights of the world, Christ's disciples, shall be no longer, destroying those things which the malice of dæmons hatches. Ofttimes in Israel famines and pestilences were caused by sin, and removed by the prayers of the Saints. (1 Kings 17:1. Jer. 14. James 5:17, 18.) Well is that said, In divers places, for God will not destroy the whole race of men at once, but judging them in portions, He gives opportunity of repentance. But if some stop be not put to these evils in their commencement, they will progress to worse, as it follows, These all are the beginnings of sorrows, that is, sorrows common to the whole world, and those which are to come upon the wicked who shall be tormented in most sharp pains.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
For nation shall rise up against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there shall be famines and pestilences and earthquakes in various places; for all these are the beginnings of sorrows (24, 7. 8).

Mark has the same things, but adds "and tumults"; Luke likewise has these same things, but adds "and there shall be terrors from heaven and great signs and storms". Let us first expound the simple and bodily meaning of the passage. For just as bodies fall sick before their death — the bodies, that is, of those who suffer no violence from outside — and just as in all cases it is through weakness that the way is made for separating the soul from its body, so also such and so great a creature as the world, when it has begun to be corrupted, as having, as it were, a beginning and an end (since "the things that are seen are temporal", and since "heaven and earth shall pass away"), must necessarily grow feeble before its corruption; so that the earth indeed is more frequently shaken and shattered by earthquakes, while the air, conceiving a certain disease-bearing force, becomes pestilential; and further still, the vital power of the earth, suddenly failing, chokes off the crops, and the generative power that produces every kind of tree, failing, chokes them off as well. Therefore, when these things happen, it follows that the movable nature also — being constituted, as it were, as some part of the whole world — must necessarily suffer along with the change of all things: for instance, not taking again its accustomed nourishment of foods, it comes to failure and is corrupted. For the heavens "shall perish", since "they shall grow old like a garment", and "whatever grows old and ages is near to destruction". It follows, then, that on account of the scarcity of foods men are stirred up to greed and to wars against those who do not suffer so great a scarcity; and that, by comparison with others who abound in the necessities of life, uprisings of some against others arise, and nation fights against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And it is possible that, together with the lack of other things, there should also come to be a lack of men possessing good sense, so that through this a tranquil and peaceful life is not found among many, but uprisings and quarrels and disturbances arise — sometimes indeed on account of greed, sometimes on account of the lust for rule, sometimes also on account of an insane craving for vainglory, and sometimes too through the desire for the vainglory of rulers, who are not content with their own kingdom, but wish to extend their own dominion and to subject many nations to themselves.

author: Origen of Alexandria
quote:
But someone will offer a still deeper explanation of the things that are to happen before the consummation of the world, and above all concerning the wars. For just as the coming of Christ made peace by divine power among very many nations — according to what the prophet says of him: "justice shall arise in his days, and abundance of peace until the moon be exalted" — and so the peace of the world was multiplied on account of the increases of the churches that were to come, in order that this peace might become an occasion of salvation for many, since they are not compelled to go out to wars and to fight for their homelands as formerly used to happen: so it follows also that, when on account of the abundance of iniquity "the love of many" has grown cold, and God and his Christ have for that reason forsaken them, wars come to pass once more — namely because the operations that sow wars are not prohibited by holiness, but are rather still further nourished on account of the ever-increasing malice of men — so that the cause of all the evils that befall is said to be those who did indeed come to the word, but afterward "all turned aside and together were made unprofitable" amid worldly evils. For as long as the salt of the earth stands firm — those to whom the Lord said: "you are the salt of the earth" — all things hold together, seasoned by the salt; but after the salt itself has become tasteless, then (to speak according to the Scripture) the very things that were salted by it, being as it were unsalted, become insipid, are corrupted and stink and are dissolved. And further, as long as the "light of the world" stands firm, all things are set aright, ordered by its clear illumination; but when this very light has been diminished in the souls of men — since it is not nourished by its proper and natural food — then, with darkness taking possession of all things, when all things have been brought into sorrow and calamities, there will come to be as it were an assembly of the adversary powers over all things, since they are not forbidden by the saints and by Christ in them, who used to forbid them, but as though in the darkness, without any prohibition, they will work in the hearts of men, so that they stir up nation against nation and kingdom against kingdom. And if (as some are also pleased to hold) famines and pestilences too come about from operations of this kind and from the angels of Satan, then likewise famines and pestilences will at that time grow strong from the adversary powers, when the disciples of Christ are no longer the salt of the earth and the light of the world — they who are the princes of God's power, destroying in men the wars that the adversary powers make, and all the things that are sown from their malice.

And at one time indeed in Israel famines and pestilences used to come about on account of sins and droughts, which the prayers of the saints dissolved — those of Samuel, of Jeremiah, and of others like them. And it is well put: there shall be famines and pestilences and earthquakes in divers places. For God does not will to destroy the human race all at once, but judging it by parts, little by little, while famines and pestilences and earthquakes come about in divers places, he grants a place for repentance to those who are amended by slight chastisements and are converted to God.
